ToolHeader.title: Number to Words in Uzbek
ToolHeader.description: Write any amount in Uzbek words — Latin and Cyrillic at the same time. Made for invoices and contracts.

result.title: Result
result.empty: Enter a number — the words appear here.
result.fractionIgnored: The fractional part is only spelled out as tiyin in “So'm” mode.

errors.invalid: That does not look like a number. Use digits, spaces, commas or dots only.
errors.tooLarge: That number is too large — up to 18 digits can be named.

why.question: Why write an amount in words?
why.answer: Invoices, contracts and payment orders carry the amount twice: in digits and in words. The written form cannot be altered afterwards, which protects the document and also catches a typo in the digits.

scripts.question: Why both Latin and Cyrillic?
scripts.answer: Documents in Uzbekistan are kept in both scripts — one office asks for Latin, another for Cyrillic. Giving both at once means not coming back for the second one. The Cyrillic column comes from Webiston's own transliteration library.

birMing.question: Why does it write «bir ming» rather than «ming»?
birMing.answer: Spoken Uzbek drops the leading «bir» — a thousand is just «ming». Written documents count every unit: 1 000 is «bir ming so'm», 100 is «bir yuz so'm». Uzbek legislation itself uses this form («bir yuz ellik baravari» on lex.uz), because a sum on a document has to read back unambiguously.

tiyin.question: How is the fractional part written?
tiyin.answer: It is read as tiyin: 1250000.50 becomes “bir million ikki yuz ellik ming so'm ellik tiyin”. A zero tiyin is left out, because carrying “nol tiyin” on every invoice is noise. In plain-number mode the fraction is not spelled out at all — Uzbek reads decimals as fractions with a denominator that changes with the number of places, and getting that subtly wrong on a document is worse than declining it.

limit.question: What is the largest number it can name?
limit.answer: Eighteen digits, up to kvadrillion. Anything larger is refused rather than half-named. The arithmetic runs on exact integers, so a long sum is never rounded.

privacy.question: Is the amount I type sent anywhere?
privacy.answer: No. Everything runs in your browser and nothing is exchanged with a server. Close the page and the number is gone.
